newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Michelin jacks up pre-exceptional profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Michelin jacks up pre-exceptional profit.

text.p: Tyremaker Michelin said on Tuesday that profit excluding tax and exceptionals items rose 50 percent to 2.88 billion francs ($561 million) in the first six months of the year, boosted by higher sales and lower production costs.
Net profit, however, fell 10 percent to 1.35 billion francs in the first half after Michelin took a 709 million franc charge to restructure its Spanish subsidiary to cuts its costs further.
Investors focused on the big underlying profit gains and drove the share price up 2.65 percent to 267 francs at midday on a weak Paris bourse.
"They were very good figures. Brokers are upgrading (their recommendations)...the message is very positive," a trader said.
Michelin's operating profit rose 31 percent to 3.62 billion francs, helped by productivity gains and tyre price increases set last year after rubber prices soared.

Finance Director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere told a news conference that raw materials prices had fallen four percent in the first half of the year and the benefits would show up in the second-half results.
The first-half results were also helped by lower interest rates, which reduced its financial expenses even though the debt grew because of a sudden buildup in inventories in the summer.
"We overestimated the demand in Europe, particularly in trucks," Bourdais de Charbonniere said.
Michelin is the world's second largest-tyremaker after Japan's Bridgestone, according to the Tire Business trade journal.
The French company's sales rose 5.4 percent to 34.91 billion francs as growth in Asian and Latin American sales offset weakness in the European and U.S. markets.
It has 18 percent of the global market in car, truck, airplane, tractor and other tyres, compared with Bridgestone's 19 percent and U.S. company Goodyear's 15 percent.

The company declined to give a profit forecast but Bourdais de Charbonniere said it did not dispute analysts' estimates, compiled before the first-half results, for a profit between three and 3.5 billion francs.

Michelin's debt at the end of June stood at 23.2 billion francs, compared with 21.6 billion a year earlier, but Bourdais de Charbonniere said debt at the end of August was below August 1995 levels, "so we're moving in the right direction".
He said the company's long-term objectives include a desire to expand in Asia. "We're under-represented in this region."
Asia has good growth potential -- particularly for truck tyres, as road transport represents a bigger share of total transport in emerging economies than in developed ones, he said.
Further geographic diversification also dovetails with Michelin's aim to reduce cyclical fluctuations.

Its exposure to the European industry cycle has been reduced by its important U.S. activities, including Goodrich, which generate a third of Michelin's turnover. Europe still accounts for 55 percent. ($1=5.137 French Franc)
